## Acquisition and read depth

| Source | Read this turn | Evidence and limit |
|---|---|---|
| [Smartpigai post](https://x.com/Smartpigai/status/2116168908722028993) | Full public post text through browser | Secondary commentary; embedded media not inspected |
| [AnnatarXBT post](https://x.com/AnnatarXBT/status/2116256966381301780) | Full public post text through browser | Primary projects resolved independently; employment and experiment-count claims not verified |
| [Linked Buzzoni guide](https://x.com/Mr_Buzzoni/status/2115443090068516935) | Full article text through browser | Practical proposal; earnings, pricing, latency and savings claims not qualified |
| [Memory Tax: Dissecting the Net Value of Agent Memory](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34073v1) | Introduction, main result table, diagnostic sections, design implications, baseline and metric details | Paper reviewed selectively, not replicated |
| [MemoryTax: The Bitter Lesson of Agent Memory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29823) | Abstract | Different paper: one conversation, one run per cell; caption visibility confounds part of the comparison |
| [Librarian Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22273) | Abstract | Trained builder using reinforcement learning; not evidence that a prompted nightly curator reproduces its gains |
| [Anthropic graph cookbook](https://platform.claude.com/cookbook/capabilities-knowledge-graph-guide) | Setup, extraction overview, query example, evaluation and scaling sections | API example, not an installed subscription-compatible integration |
| [Karpathy autoresearch](https://github.com/karpathy/autoresearch) and [program.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karpathy/autoresearch/master/program.md) | README mechanism and experiment instructions | Pattern reference; no GPU experiment run |
| [Karpathy llm-wiki](https://gist.github.com/karpathy/442a6bf555914893e9891c11519de94f) | Complete idea file, excluding comment-thread claims | Method proposal, not measured harness efficacy |
| [TypeSafe System One](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api/system-one) | API request/response and authorization schema | Identifies Jev; no account, install or API invocation |

## Findings

## Findings

The broader Memory Tax paper compares eleven memory systems with a substantial
raw-history retrieval baseline: BM25 plus dense search and reranking, optionally
two rounds. Its diagnosis distinguishes information loss, retrieval difficulty
and reader/writer model changes. Source recovery alongside derived memory is a
useful design lead. This does not establish our local system's performance or
prove structured memory universally inferior. See its main table and sections
4, 6 and A.2 at the linked paper.

The smaller MemoryTax paper is a separate study, not a replication of that
eleven-system comparison. Its abstract explicitly discloses narrow sampling and
unequal photo-caption availability. Keep those limits attached to its headline.

The cookbook demonstrates extraction, entity resolution and graph-backed
answers. Its relation scorer ignores predicate wording; use that as a warning
against treating entity connectivity as relationship correctness. It requires an
Anthropic API key. Reuse methodology without assuming the example runs through
Claude Max authentication.

Autoresearch separates an editable training file from fixed evaluation, uses a
fixed experiment duration and keeps a results ledger. Transfer the experimental
discipline, not its unbounded loop or permission-disabling recommendation.

The llm-wiki idea preserves original sources and maintains a linked derived wiki
with an index and chronological log. It offers a useful human-readable view;
the source itself calls the tooling optional and domain-dependent.

Jev is now concretely identified: TypeSafe documents a remote decision endpoint
with named questions, typed answers, effective model and usage fields. A typed
response is not evidence of calibrated routing quality, local inference, privacy
equivalence or net token savings.

def search_shared_documents(root, *, vault_id, manifest, manifest_sha256, allowed_ids, query,
                            backend="lexical", max_results=5, max_bytes=8192, context_lines=0):
    """Filter approved IDs before reading/scoring; resolve every returned excerpt by its pin.

    Caller-supplied allowed_ids is an explicit scope, not an authentication service. BM25 scores
    express lexical overlap, not answer confidence. A zero-overlap query abstains; missing/stale
    approved evidence is an error. This pilot caps each scope at 100 notes and total text at 4 MiB.
    Opt-in neighbouring lines retain local qualifications; they do not guarantee a complete
    answer. The byte cap admits a whole requested window or records its omission.
    """
    if not isinstance(vault_id, str) or not vault_id.strip():
        raise ValueError("shared vault identity is required")
    if (not isinstance(allowed_ids, list) or len(allowed_ids) > 100
            or any(not isinstance(identity, str) or not identity or len(identity) > 256 for identity in allowed_ids)
            or len(set(allowed_ids)) != len(allowed_ids)):
        raise ValueError("scope must contain at most 100 unique document IDs")
    if not isinstance(query, str) or not query.strip() or len(query) > 512:
        raise ValueError("query must be nonempty and at most 512 characters")

## Architecture: implemented boundaries versus claims

| Layer | Inspected evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Task dependency graph | `workgraph/plan.py`, leases and command gates | Execution state; not a graph of research knowledge |
| Source/capability map | [source-evidence-graph.md](../v1/source-evidence-graph.md) explicitly says research evidence, not installed functionality | Useful curated table; not proof of an operational whole-corpus graph |
| Document/KB search | `mcp/kb.py`: scoped document sections, BM25 and FTS5 | Implemented lexical retrieval; not semantic or graph traversal |
| Shared document retrieval | `vault_retrieval.py`: explicit allowed IDs, pinned manifest, lexical/FTS5, bounded excerpts | Opt-in pilot, at most 100 documents/4 MiB per scope; no persistent graph in this module |
| Source and record integrity | `vault_sources.py`, `project_memory.py`; immutable receipts, revisions, pending assertions, withdrawal/history | Valuable correctness foundation; not automatic truth checking of arbitrary prose |
| Conversation inventory | `source_inventory.py` inspects transcript metadata/index progress | Different denominator from shared web links; byte coverage is not semantic extraction |
| Handoffs and cold recovery | Existing source/process tests and bounded native receipts | Partial evidence; not lossless memory or universal client compliance |
| Learning/discovery | `procedures.py`, `improve.py`, `discovery_cycle.py` | Candidate generation and held promotion; daily discovery covers two approved model-document URLs, not the entire ecosystem |

The architecture's separation of authoritative originals, derived indexes,
project/task state and optional learned procedures is a sensible baseline for
the stated requirements. It still needs operational integration and evidence.
Changing Python to Rust, adding a graph database, or increasing agent count does
not by itself close a missing-content or missing-evaluation gap.

def test_pending_claim_is_not_a_normal_search_or_recovery_hit(tmp_path):
    project_id = initialize(tmp_path)
    (tmp_path / "source.txt").write_text("Port: 8081\n")
    source = SourceVault(tmp_path, project_id).capture("source.txt")
    store = ProjectMemory(tmp_path, project_id)
    item = {"id": "service-port", "project_id": project_id, "layer": "project_facts", "kind": "fact",
            "scope": "project", "text": "Port: 9999", "provenance": [
                {"source": source, "start_line": 1, "end_line": 1}], "confidence": "verified",
            "sensitivity": "internal", "access_boundary": "local_user", "owner": "fixture",
            "freshness": "current"}
    receipt = store.append(item, expected=None)
    policy = {"allowed_sensitivities": ["internal"], "allowed_scopes": ["project"],
              "layers": ["project_facts"]}
    results = store.search("service-port", **policy)
    assert not results["hits"]
    assert {entry["reason"] for entry in results["omitted"]} == {"pending"}
    recovered = store.recover(receipt, phase="resume", depends_on_memory=True,
                              verified_receipt=receipt, **policy)
    assert recovered["decision"] == "HOLD" and recovered["reason"] == "pending"
    assert "record" not in recovered
    exact = store.read_scoped(receipt, **policy)
    assert exact["kind"] == "pending-memory-data"
    assert exact["usable_for_current_decisions"] is False
    page = store.search_page("service-port", **policy)
    assert page["hits"] == []
    assert {entry["reason"] for entry in page["omitted"]} == {"pending"}
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="pending memory"):
        store.read(receipt, allowed_sensitivities=["internal"])
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="pending memory"):
        store.latest("service-port", allowed_sensitivities=["internal"])

def bind_hold(home, project, identity, task_id, task, answer,
              base_artifact, candidate_artifact, base_usage, candidate_usage):

    Exact-byte correctness is a narrow mechanical grader, not general quality.
    The provided native receipts are checked for completeness and hashed, but
    same-user mutation and actor answer isolation are not established here.
    """
    project = _scope(project)
    task_sha, answer_sha = _bytes(task, "task"), _bytes(answer, "answer")
    base_sha = _bytes(base_artifact, "baseline artifact")
    cand_sha = _bytes(candidate_artifact, "candidate artifact")
    base_tokens, cand_tokens = _native_tokens(base_usage), _native_tokens(candidate_usage)
    with _db(home) as con:
        payload = _proposal(con, project, identity)
        frozen = con.execute("SELECT task_sha256,answer_sha256 FROM procedure_frozen_cases "
                             "WHERE id=? AND task_id=?", (identity, task_id)).fetchone()
        if not frozen or (task_sha, answer_sha) != tuple(frozen):
            raise ValueError("frozen task or answer receipt is missing or changed")
        grader = {"version": "exact-bytes-v1",
                  "sha256": hashlib.sha256(Path(__file__).read_bytes()).hexdigest()}
        result = {"schema": 1, "project": project, "procedure_id": identity,
                  "candidate_sha256": payload["sha256"], "task_id": task_id,
                  "task_sha256": task_sha, "answer_sha256": answer_sha,

            raise ValueError("binder receipt conflicts with changed artifact, usage or grader")
